framework: IEEE 2802-2022 IEEE Standard for Performance and Safety Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Based Medical Devices: Terminology
requirement_paraphrase: The catalogue description says the standard establishes concepts and terminology for performance and safety evaluation of AI based medical devices, covering technology, datasets, quality characteristics and quality evaluation, with an annex of basic equations for quality evaluation.
what_is_tested: Performance and safety of AI based medical devices (terminology only)

framework: ETSI EN 304 223 V2.1.1 Securing Artificial Intelligence (SAI); Baseline Cyber Security Requirements for AI Models and Systems
requirement_paraphrase: Recommended: treat a major update as a new model version and undertake a new security testing and evaluation process for it.

framework: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems (G7; date not stated in the text received)
requirement_paraphrase: Organizations should use diverse internal and independent external testing measures, including adversarial testing, and apply suitable mitigations for identified risks; testing should occur in secure environments and at several checkpoints, in particular before deployment and market placement.
what_is_tested: Advanced AI systems across risks, using red teaming and other measures
who_tests: Developing organisations, with independent external testers

framework: International AI Safety Report, Second Key Update: Technical Safeguards and Risk Management (25 November 2025)
clause_or_page: Section 2 Technical methods, 'Sophisticated attackers routinely find ways...' (no page numbers in text read)
requirement_paraphrase: Describes adversarial training, where developers create attacks that try to elicit harmful behaviour, and says it remains imperfect: attackers keep devising new attacks that succeed, and safeguards are hard to evaluate under realistic conditions.
what_is_tested: Robustness of safeguards to adversarial attack (jailbreaks, prompt injection)
who_tests: Developers (adversarial training and attack generation), as described

framework: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development: Guiding Principles (FDA, Health Canada, MHRA; October 2021)
clause_or_page: Principle 8, 'Testing Demonstrates Device Performance During Clinically Relevant Conditions'
requirement_paraphrase: Test plans should be statistically sound and produce clinically relevant performance data independent of the training data, taking into account the intended population, important subgroups and confounders.
what_is_tested: Machine learning enabled medical device performance under clinically relevant conditions

framework: Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence Safety Assurance, Version I (FAA; issue date not stated in the text read)
clause_or_page: Section 'Application of Principles to Aircraft Certification', p. 16
requirement_paraphrase: Cites extensive stress testing of AI systems at item level to verify functionality, with further tests at system and aircraft level to address failure analysis.
what_is_tested: Learned AI at item, system and aircraft level

framework: SR 11-7, Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (dated 4 April 2011, last updated 19 August 2011 per page)
clause_or_page: Section 'Model Validation', independence passage (locator not seen)
requirement_paraphrase: Validation should involve a degree of independence from model development and use, generally performed by staff not responsible for development or use.
who_tests: Bank staff independent of development and use

framework: Principles for the Secure Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Operational Technology (CISA, ASD ACSC and partners, initial version 3 December 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Treat AI systems like any new OT system and test them for safety impacts such as latency and interoperability, using test infrastructure before production deployment where possible, and provide failsafe reversion to traditional automation or manual control.
what_is_tested: Safety impact (latency, interoperability) and failsafe reversion

framework: Good machine learning practice for medical device development: guiding principles (MHRA, FDA, Health Canada; GOV.UK page showing 'Updated 5 October 2026', first published 27 October 2021)
clause_or_page: Guiding principle 4 (Training data sets are independent of test sets)
requirement_paraphrase: Training and test datasets should be selected and maintained to be appropriately independent, with all sources of dependence (such as patient, acquisition and site factors) addressed.
what_is_tested: Independence of test data from training data

framework: NSW AI Assessment Framework (Digital NSW page, copyright 2026; no version number or update date seen)
clause_or_page: Section 'When to submit your project to the AI Review Committee'
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems whose self-assessment gives a high or critical risk must be submitted to the AI Secretariat for review by the AI Review Committee.
what_is_tested: Risk assessed through the AIAF self-assessment; committee review of high and critical risk systems
who_tests: NSW Government agencies (self-assessment), then AI Review Committee via AI Secretariat

framework: AI Discussion Paper (AIディスカッションペーパー) version 1.0, Financial Services Agency, March 2025 (summary PDF)
requirement_paraphrase: Says a consistent framework is needed to detect and address model bias early; notes that evaluation indicators and audit procedures are not yet clearly defined.

framework: Review of Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices (機械学習を活用する医療機器の審査について), material 4, PMDA expert committee on AI-based software medical devices, undated
requirement_paraphrase: Warns that reusing evaluation data may lead to unnoticed optimisation to that data; suggests safeguards: check generalisation on a small separate dataset, cap the number of uses of the evaluation data, and set a model improvement process that assumes reuse.

framework: Consumer Protection in respect of Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence, HKMA circular dated 19 August 2024 (as stated in the fetched text)
requirement_paraphrase: Institutions should consider preventing unfair bias, including by adjusting to remove bias during the validation and review process, anonymising some data categories and using representative datasets.
